role_label: hydrolysis-driven pH modifier / anion structure-directing agent
mechanism_description: Fe3+ undergoes strong hydrolysis in water, releasing H+ and progressively lowering solution pH, which controls nucleation/growth kinetics of iron oxide/oxyhydroxide phases; the accompanying Cl- ions can also be incorporated into or adsorb on developing structures (e.g., akaganeite tunnels, anisotropic hematite/goethite growth), acting as a mineralizer or morphology-directing anion.
search_query: FeCl3 hydrolysis pH control morphology iron oxide hematite akaganeite chloride structure-directing
